# **Comprehensive Analysis of FreeCAD-to-URDF Exporters: Architecture, Licensing, and Commercial Viability**

> **Verification notes (2026-10-09).** The two GitHub repository pages were checked:
> - **CROSS** (galou/freecad.cross): license shown as **LGPL-2.1**, compatible with FreeCAD **v0.21.2 or later**. Matches this report.
> - **RobotCAD** (drfenixion/freecad.robotcad): license shown as **LGPL-2.1**. Matches. It advertises "automatic calculation (based on material or custom mass)" of mass, inertia and centre of mass, and ROS 2 package generation with launchers for Gazebo, RViz and PX4.
> - **Correction:** `ros2_controllers` integration is listed under RobotCAD's **"External Extended Code Generator"**, not the basic generator. Check whether that external generator is open source and runs locally before relying on it.
> - **Correction:** RobotCAD's stated minimum version is inconsistent on its own page ("at least v0.21.2", "v1 or above", recommended 1.1.x AppImage, Python 3.12+ inside FreeCAD). Treat FreeCAD 1.1 with Python 3.12+ as the practical requirement.
> - Not verified: the claim that CROSS lacks automatic inertia computation, and the commit-count comparison between the forks. Neither license label says whether it is "-only" or "-or-later".

In modern robotics engineering, bridging the gap between Computer-Aided Design (CAD) platforms and simulation environments represents a critical operational bottleneck1. FreeCAD has established itself as the leading open-source parametric 3D CAD modeling system, heavily utilized for mechanical component design, kinematic structuring, and physical layout1. However, executing physics-based dynamic simulations in frameworks such as ROS, ROS 2, Gazebo, RViz, or Isaac Sim requires representing mechanical assemblies as Unified Robot Description Format (URDF) or Simulation Description Format (SDF) files2. URDF files encode topological link-joint trees, spatial transformations, visual geometries, collision bounds, and mass-inertial matrices2.  
Exporting CAD data to URDF requires mapping parametric constraints and solid body geometries into structured XML specifications and polygon meshes2. While proprietary CAD suites rely on commercial plugins such as the SolidWorks URDF Exporter, the open-source FreeCAD ecosystem relies on community-developed workbenches and Python macros5. Evaluating the architectural capabilities, open-source licenses, commercial viability, and performance trade-offs of existing FreeCAD-to-URDF exporters highlights how these tools facilitate commercial robotics deployment2.

## **Technical Overview of FreeCAD URDF Exporters**

The ecosystem of FreeCAD tools designed for URDF generation has evolved from basic macro-based mesh conversion scripts into complex workbenches capable of end-to-end software-in-the-loop package generation2. The primary active tools in this domain are CROSS (galou/freecad.cross) and its advanced fork RobotCAD (drfenixion/freecad.robotcad), supported by historical workbenches such as RobotCreator (maidenone/RobotCreator) and Assembly-based translation scripts2.

| Exporter Tool | Primary Developer | Open Source License | Target Ecosystem | Minimum FreeCAD Version | Mass & Inertial Tensor Handling | Key Architectural Features |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **CROSS** (freecad.cross) | galou | GNU LGPL-2.1 | ROS / ROS 2 | v0.21.2 | Primitive-based / External | Modular xacro macro processing, MoveIt planning scene service integration, primitive shape text export7. |
| **RobotCAD** (freecad.robotcad) | drfenixion | GNU LGPL-2.1 | ROS 2 | v1.0.0 / v1.1 AppImage | Automated volumetric density & CoM extraction | Assembly WB structure conversion, ros2\_control config generation, Gazebo sensor FOV visualization, Docker/Conda runtime support2. |
| **RobotCreator** | maidenone | Open Source (Legacy) | ROS / Gazebo | v0.16–v0.18 | Manual / Scripted | Legacy URDF/SDF tool; superseded by CROSS and RobotCAD8. |
| **Assembly4 Custom Exporters** | FreeCAD Community | GNU LGPL-2.1 (FreeCAD Core) | Generic URDF | v0.19+ | Manual via Mass WB | Maps Assembly4 Local Coordinate Systems (LCS) to URDF \<origin\> tags10. |

## **In-Depth Analysis of Exporter Architectures and Features**

### **CROSS Workbench (galou/freecad.cross)**

The CAD & ROS Open-Source Synergy (CROSS) workbench provides native ROS integration within FreeCAD, permitting modular robot description generation through direct parametric manipulation7. CROSS operates as an architectural bridge between CAD geometry and ROS workspace environments7. It processes standard geometric primitives (Part::Box, Part::Sphere, Part::Cylinder) directly into formatted URDF text blocks and manages nested xacro macro expansions7. This allows users to import modular xacro definitions, assign interactive joint parameters within FreeCAD, and visualize kinematic responses in real time7.  
CROSS provides modular assembly capabilities, allowing separate URDF and xacro files to be combined into a single workcell description using \<xacro:include\> elements and programmatic macro calls7. It interfaces with ROS node instances via the terminal, enabling features such as querying the MoveIt planning scene service (/get\_planning\_scene) to synchronize CAD layouts with live motion planning environments7.

#### **Architectural Advantages**

* **Modular Xacro Handling**: Handles complex xacro structures, parameter inputs, and hierarchical macro inclusion without flattening the model hierarchy prematurely7.  
* **Lightweight Footprint**: Operates with minimal overhead on standard FreeCAD installations (v0.21.2+) without requiring heavy external daemon stacks7.  
* **Bi-directional Previewing**: Allows setting values for actuated joints directly in the GUI to verify kinematic limits and link transformations prior to exporting7.  
* **Commercial License Flexibility**: Distributed under GNU LGPL-2.1, supporting royalty-free integration in personal, research, and commercial pipelines7.

#### **Technical Limitations**

* **Manual Inertial Assignment**: Lacks automated bulk calculation of complex ![][image1] inertial tensors from arbitrary solid meshes, relying heavily on manual entry or basic geometric primitives7.  
* **Terminal Dependency**: Sourcing ROS workspace environment variables requires launching FreeCAD via terminal flags (freecad \--module-path ...) to unlock full ROS functionality7.  
* **Limited Modern ROS 2 Scaffolding**: Does not automatically generate ros2\_control hardware interface blocks or launch file scaffolding out-of-the-box2.

### **RobotCAD Workbench (drfenixion/freecad.robotcad)**

RobotCAD represents a significant fork and evolution of CROSS, positioned over 1,000 commits ahead of the original upstream repository2. It pivots FreeCAD from a simple geometry viewer into an end-to-end code and configuration generator tailored specifically for ROS 2, Gazebo, and RViz 2 workflows2. RobotCAD addresses the friction points of manual ROS 2 package creation by automating mass-property extraction, joint frame alignment, collision geometry simplification, and control configuration generation2.

#### **Core Capabilities and Automation Engine**

* **Assembly Workbench Conversion**: RobotCAD includes built-in conversion tools that transform standard FreeCAD assembly structures (such as Assembly4) into structured RobotCAD link-joint trees2.  
* **Automated Physical Property Extraction**: By assigning physical materials or custom mass density values to CAD parts, RobotCAD automatically computes the 3D center of mass (CoM) in local and global coordinates, link mass, and the full ![][image1] moment of inertia matrix (![][image2]) relative to the link's joint origin2.  
* **Control and Sensor Integration**: Beyond URDF generation, RobotCAD outputs ready-to-use ROS 2 package directory structures, including launch scripts, RViz display profiles, Gazebo world files (.sdf), sensor field-of-view visualizers, and controller configurations based on ros2\_control2.  
* **Containerized Deployment Options**: To bypass Linux system library and Python dependency conflicts, RobotCAD provides Docker containers and Conda packages containing FreeCAD 1.1 AppImages pre-configured with ROS 2 runtimes2.

#### **Architectural Advantages**

* **Complete ROS 2 Pipeline**: Generates full, launchable ROS 2 packages rather than isolated URDF snippets2.  
* **Automated Mass and Inertia Calculations**: Eliminates manual volumetric integration and frame-shifting math by automatically deriving inertial tensors from CAD solid geometries2.  
* **Interactive Joint Placement**: Features intuitive UI tools to align joint origin frames directly by selecting topological faces, edges, or Local Coordinate Systems (LCS)2.  
* **Collision Shape Generation**: Automatically builds simplified axis-aligned bounding boxes, cylinders, or convex hulls from complex visual meshes to optimize physics engine collision checking2.

#### **Technical Limitations**

* **Strict Dependencies**: Requires FreeCAD v1.0.0 or higher and Python 3.12+ environments, making it incompatible with older LTS distributions without containerization2.  
* **Namespace Conflicts**: Shares identical module namespaces with its upstream parent, meaning CROSS and RobotCAD cannot co-exist within the same FreeCAD installation directory2.  
* **System Complexity**: The expanded feature set (AI primitive generation, multicopter PX4 launchers, agentic servers) increases the learning curve for users seeking simple geometry exports2.

### **Legacy Implementations and Assembly-Based Kinematic Mapping**

#### **RobotCreator Workbench (maidenone/RobotCreator)**

Developed in 2017, RobotCreator was an early open-source initiative designed to convert FreeCAD models into URDF and SDF representations for Gazebo8. While historically significant, the repository is unmaintained and lacks compatibility with modern FreeCAD API changes (v0.19 and above) and ROS 2 standards2. Its functionality has been absorbed and modernized by projects like CROSS and RobotCAD4.

#### **Native Assembly4 LCS Kinematic Mapping**

In the absence of dedicated exporters, engineers often construct robot kinematics using FreeCAD's Assembly4 workbench10. Assembly4 structures linkages by attaching datum features known as Local Coordinate Systems (LCS) to individual parts11. Joint translation vectors ![][image3] and Euler orientation angles (![][image4]) are derived from the transformation matrix between a parent link's attachment LCS and a child link's target LCS10. Custom Python macros iterate through the Assembly4 Model tree, extracting the relative transformation matrix ![][image5]:  
![][image6]  
This matrix is converted into the standard URDF \<origin xyz="x y z" rpy="roll pitch yaw"/\> format, while mesh exporter macros save visual components as separate STL or Collada (.dae) files8.

## **Licensing Analysis and Commercial Viability**

Evaluating software licensing is critical when integrating open-source CAD exporters into commercial product development pipelines2. Both primary active workbenches, CROSS and RobotCAD, are distributed under the GNU Lesser General Public License v2.1 (LGPL-2.1)2. FreeCAD itself is governed by LGPL-2.1+ for its core libraries8.

### **Legal Mechanics for Commercial Engineering**

Under standard software intellectual property frameworks, using an LGPL-2.1 licensed authoring tool to generate data files (such as XML URDF documents, XACRO macros, or STL/DAE 3D mesh files) does not infect the resulting data files with the LGPL license2. The exported files are produced data outputs rather than derivative works of the exporter's Python code base2. Consequently, commercial entities retain full, unencumbered proprietary copyright over all exported robot description packages and mechanical designs2.  
Commercial companies may freely install, deploy, and execute CROSS or RobotCAD across internal engineering workstations, automated CI/CD conversion runners, and internal Docker infrastructure without paying licensing royalties or disclosing proprietary CAD geometries2. However, if a commercial firm modifies the internal Python source code of CROSS or RobotCAD itself and subsequently distributes those modified workbench binaries or scripts externally to clients or third parties, the modified exporter source code must be made available under the terms of LGPL-2.12. If modifications remain purely internal to the enterprise, there is no obligation to publish the modified code base2.

## **Technical Trade-offs and Engineering Best Practices**

Transitioning mechanical assemblies from CAD parametric space into software description formats exposes core technical trade-offs across coordinate systems, mesh fidelity, and physical dynamics2.

| Engineering Dimension | Parametric CAD Domain | Simulation Description Domain | Primary Technical Trade-off |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Spatial Alignment** | B-REP Solids & Mating Constraints | Tree-Structured Joint Transforms (\<origin\>) | CAD origins rarely coincide with rotation axes; requires explicit Local Coordinate System anchoring2. |
| **Dynamic Modeling** | Volume Integration (![][image7]) | Mass, CoM, and ![][image8] Inertial Tensor Matrix | Automated density integration is highly accurate but susceptible to errors from hollow bodies or unmodeled fasteners2. |
| **Geometric Mesh Fidelity** | Parametric STEP / Nurb Surfaces | Polygon Visual (.dae) & Collision Bounds | High-resolution visual meshes preserve aesthetic detail but severely degrade real-time physics engine performance if used for collisions2. |
| **Control Integration** | Static Geometry & Kinematic Chains | ros2\_control Interfaces & Joint Actuators | Basic URDF exporters omit control scaffolding, requiring manual authoring of hardware interfaces and controller configurations2. |

### **Coordinate Systems and Spatial Alignment**

Parametric CAD platforms define geometry via boundary representation solids referenced to global or local origin points1. URDF requires explicit parent-to-child joint transformations2. Direct export of raw CAD parts frequently leads to frame misalignment because CAD origin points rarely coincide with physical joint rotation axes5. Modern workbenches enforce explicit frame anchoring, where tools like RobotCAD extract transformation offsets between parent face anchors and child reference points, ensuring joint rotation vectors align with mechanical pivot points2.

### **Volumetric Mass Properties vs. Inertial Approximations**

Physics simulation engines require accurate mass (![][image9]), center of mass (![][image10]), and a positive-definite inertial tensor matrix (![][image11]) to yield realistic dynamic behaviors2:  
![][image12]  
While CROSS relies on primitive geometric shapes where moments of inertia are analytically calculated, RobotCAD performs automated numeric integration over CAD solid volumes based on assigned material density matrices2. This yields accurate mass properties directly from complex geometries, provided that CAD models exclude non-physical overlaps or unmodeled hollow spaces that could distort computed mass properties2.

### **Visual Tessellation vs. Collision Mesh Complexity**

Exporting CAD models to simulation platforms requires converting solid geometries into polygon meshes, typically STL or Collada .dae formats14. Exporting CAD solids at high tessellation density yields accurate visual renders in RViz, but slows down collision detection engines if used directly for physics checks2. RobotCAD addresses this trade-off by decoupling visual meshes from collision geometries, automatically generating low-polygon bounding boxes, spheres, cylinders, or convex hulls for collision checking while retaining detailed high-resolution meshes for visual rendering2.

## **Strategic Synthesis and Recommendations**

Selecting an appropriate FreeCAD URDF exporter depends on project architecture, target ROS versions, and the required depth of simulation automation2.

> 1. **Adopt RobotCAD for End-to-End ROS 2 Deployments**: For engineering teams building modern ROS 2 pipelines, RobotCAD provides the most complete feature set2. Its automated material density calculation, collision mesh generation, and ros2\_control scaffolding significantly reduce manual authoring effort2.  
> 2. **Utilize CROSS for Modular Xacro Workcells**: For projects that rely on pre-existing xacro macro libraries or require real-time integration with MoveIt planning scenes without full ROS 2 package generation, CROSS remains a lightweight and effective option7.  
> 3. **Establish Standardized CAD Frame Conventions**: Regardless of the chosen exporter, engineering teams should mandate explicit Local Coordinate System anchoring at all mechanical pivot points during early parametric modeling2. This practice ensures consistent joint origin exports and eliminates manual transformation adjustments downstream2.  
> 4. **Isolate Workbenches in Containerized Runtimes**: Due to software dependency requirements (such as FreeCAD 1.0+ and Python 3.12+ for RobotCAD), organizations should leverage pre-built Docker containers or Conda archives to ensure reproducible build pipelines across developer workstations2.
